summary.headline: Sugs Lloyd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR78.4 crore with EBITDA margin 15.3%; order book INR807 crore; FY28 INR1,000 crore target reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR78.40 crore, up 32% YoY, with EBITDA of about INR12 crore (15.3% margin, up 32 bps) and PAT of INR7.5 crore (up 30%). Management attributed the slower quarter to Patna project teething issues and supplier material shortages that pushed some June billing into Q2. Order book stood at INR807 crore (ex-GST) as of 30 June, and management reaffirmed the INR600 crore FY27 and INR1,000 crore FY28 revenue targets. Receivables fell by about INR10 crore to INR149 crore, while borrowings rose from INR68 crore to INR91 crore to fund Patna working capital.

financial_highlights.change: +32% YoY (vs INR59.41 crore in Q1 FY26)
Higher YoY, attributed to working capital build

financial_highlights.metric: Power T&D and smart grid revenue
financial_highlights.change: vs INR16.34 crore in Q1 FY26 (27% share)
Up from INR50 crore, funded from internal accruals

segments.name: Power transmission, distribution and smart grid (incl. FPI)
segments.commentary: INR46.32 crore in Q1, ~59% of revenue. Fault passage indicator (FPI) is described as the fastest-growing niche, with >50% domestic share; Q1 FPI order wins already exceed the full FY26 product order value per management.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: INR32 crore in Q1, ~41% of revenue. Shifting toward RESCO and capex-plus-RESCO mandates with 10-year service contracts; first such order is Bihar PM-Surya Ghar at INR56 crore.

segments.name: Products / other (target)
segments.commentary: Management targets products at ~10% of revenue by FY28. No product revenue split disclosed for Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR600 crore reiterated as on track; Q1 slippage expected to be recovered in Q2.
FY28 revenue target of INR1,000 crore reaffirmed; management says it needs unexecuted order book of INR2,000-2,500 crore to deliver it.
EBITDA margin expected to be sustained at around current levels for FY27 and FY28; EPC margins to dilute with scale, offset by product mix.
Peak borrowing for FY27 estimated at around INR130 crore at a cost of about 9%.
BESS and transmission expected to contribute from H2 FY27 and FY28; BESS guidance treated as incremental to the INR600/1,000 crore targets.
capex_capacity: VCBs and RMUs require additional capex; quantum and funding not yet formalised. FPI needs no incremental capex.
Compact FPI at advanced stage, targeted launch in roughly 2-3 months if technology partnership materialises; VCB roll-out may take about a year including type tests; RMU at initial stage.
Transmission entry expected through final-stage tenders; first breakthrough to be announced soon.
BESS: re-entering with small, distributed projects; tenders identified in Rajasthan and Bihar; bids to be submitted shortly.
Management says it is fully resourced for FY27 and FY28 INR1,000 crore target with sanctioned financing in place.
demand_pricing: Order book INR807 crore (ex-GST) at 30 June, ~2.7x FY26 revenue of ~INR300 crore; management cites ~18-24 months visibility, mostly repeat customers.
Q1 fresh awards INR58.37 crore across three states: Bihar PM-Surya Ghar INR56 crore (RESCO), Odisha FPI order (75-day delivery), and Madhya Pradesh FPI order INR3.37 crore with 5 years AMC.

Qualified bid pipeline INR1,350 crore; tenders at final stage exceed INR1,200 crore. Of the INR1,200 crore, ~INR70 crore awarded so far, rest under evaluation, with a 1-2 month wait; management guides 15-20% strike rate.
New-state strike rate ~10-15% vs 30-40% on prior exposure, per management's answer; JV and PSU back-to-back models used where eligibility is not met.
Receivable days are long: management cites ~180 debtor days across the sector; collections improving via TReDS, purchase invoice discounting and surety bonds in place of bank guarantees.
International exploration at an early stage; Africa opportunities being explored, no Sri Lanka opportunity seen.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 15.3% margins sustainable, what consolidated margins to expect through FY28-FY29, and what closing order book is expected by year end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of sustaining margins, helped by the growing product business; product orders received in Q1 already match the full FY26 product order value. Closing order book was not quantified: management pointed to INR1,350 crore qualified pipeline and said booking orders is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR1,200 crore final-stage tender pipeline has been won, and what strike rate applies?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR70 crore awarded so far, with the rest under evaluation for another one to two months. Management guided a 15-20% strike rate; the analyst's 20-25% framing was corrected to 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables after Q1 and why Q1 growth was only 30% against a INR600 crore FY27 target that implies 100% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade receivables were INR149 crore. Slowdown attributed to Patna teething issues and supplier material shortages that pushed June billing into Q2; management called it deferment, not shortfall, and reaffirmed the INR600 crore FY27 target.

qa_highlights.question: Expected segment split at INR1,000 crore revenue, and product share?
qa_highlights.answer: Power T&D about 40-45% and solar about 40-45%, with the remaining ~10% from other businesses including products. Products targeted at ~10% of revenue by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How do new-state entry, qualification and win rates work, and what is the timeline to repeat orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Eligibility is technical and financial; gaps are filled via JVs or a PSU back-to-back model. New-state strike rate is about 10-15% versus 30-40% on existing exposure. Order book visibility is 18-24 months, mostly repeat customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses roughly double, and what is the peak debt and cost of debt for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expense levels are in line with full-year plans and revenue growth outpaces cost growth. Peak FY27 borrowing estimated at about INR130 crore at roughly 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Is BESS and transmission included in INR600/1,000 crore guidance, and what capex is needed for VCB/RMU?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS is totally new and incremental to guidance. FPI needs no capex; VCBs and RMUs need additional capex, not yet formalised or funded. VCB roll-out may take about a year including type tests.

risks_watch: Receivables still high at INR149 crore with sector debtor days around 180; collections depend on government payment cycles and treasury closures.

Borrowings rose from INR68 crore to INR91 crore; management guides peak FY27 debt near INR130 crore and debt/equity capped at 1.1-1.2x, so working-capital intensity could pressure finance costs and margins.
FY27 INR600 crore revenue needs H2 ramp; Q1 slippage of June billing into Q2 and supplier material shortages must be recovered.
FY28 INR1,000 crore target requires unexecuted order book of INR2,000-2,500 crore versus INR807 crore now; closing order book by FY27 end was not quantified.
Tender win rates: ~INR70 crore of INR1,200 crore final-stage tenders awarded so far, with new-state strike rates of 10-15%.
New segments (transmission, BESS, VCB/RMU, compact FPI) have no confirmed timelines, funding or orders yet; compact FPI launch depends on an uncertain technology partnership.
key_quotes: Our customer collection during the quarter was INR100 crores against the revenue of INR78 crores, which has helped bring trade receivables down by INR10 crores.
So, it is not short fall, it is a kind of deferment or slippage from this quarter.
Not everything is perfect yet, but it is clearly moving in the right direction.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, FY27 and FY28 targets and product pipeline, but cautious and vague on specifics such as closing order book, VCB/RMU capex and transmission timing. Management was candid about the receivables and working-capital burden, calling it a gradual process with "not everything perfect yet".

adds.what: Compact fault passage indicator (FPI) product launch, pending technology partnership
VCB and RMU product lines (capex quantum and funding not formalised)

growth.why: Management reaffirmed INR600 crore FY27 (about 100% over ~INR300 crore FY26 base) and INR1,000 crore FY28 targets, backed by INR807 crore order book (~2.7x FY26 revenue) and a qualified bid pipeline, but no new productive capacity is quantified and the FY28 target depends on INR2,000-2,500 crore of unexecuted orders still to be won against a 15-20% strike rate.
